text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

Panel composition alone is statistically unremarkable — in many ministries women dominate HR and senior policy panels, so an all-female panel of four arises often by chance. It tells you nothing about how they scored you. Raising it makes you look like you're explaining away a loss rather than contesting one, and it will colour how your written request is handled.

Your real grievance is procedural: two weeks' silence on a reasonable request for reasons. Chase that in writing, citing any internal deadline or freedom-of-information right. Ask for your scores against the published criteria.

If the reasons reveal a criterion applied inconsistently, or "international projects" wasn't in the advertised spec, you have something concrete. Composition isn't it.
